synopsis: SSIM is an image- or field-similarity metric used for sensor-model validation and requires pixel-matched pairs [f4802]. It assesses appearance and structure rather than the behavior of perception and decision software [f14791]. A physics-based radar simulator dramatically improved structural-similarity and mutual-information scores, yet a detector trained only on real radar data failed to detect most cars in the simulated images [f14793]. This result highlights a validation gap: improved similarity scores alone do not establish that simulated sensor data will support successful perception [f14791, f14793].

relations.note: Adds the pixel-matched-pair requirement for SSIM-based sensor-model validation.
Improved similarity scores alongside detection failures demonstrate the distinction between similarity and perception performance.
